    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    Bishop
    A bishop: moves any number of squares diagonally.
    Board
    The 8 x 8 grid of squares and the record of captured pieces.
    BoardEvaluator
    Scores a position for the minimax search: positive is good for the side asked about.
    BoardPanel
    Draws the 8 x 8 board and turns mouse actions into calls on the GameController.
    ChessApp
    Entry point for the interactive console chess application.
    ChessFrame
    The main window: the board in the center, a side panel with the turn indicator, game status, captured pieces, and move list, a message bar at the bottom, and a Game menu with New Game, Restart, and Exit.
    ChessGuiApp
    Entry point for the Swing chess application.
    Command
    A single parsed line of user input, produced by InputParser.
    Command.Type
    The kinds of command the console understands.
    ConsoleUI
    Text interface for the game: prints the board, reads commands, and forwards moves to Game.
    DemoDriver
    Non-interactive demonstration driver that runs labeled test scenarios against Game and InputParser, printing the input, the expected result, the observed result, and PASS/FAIL for each check.
    Difficulty
    The computer opponent's difficulty levels, each mapped to a MoveStrategy.
    Game
    Coordinates a two-player game: owns the board, the players, and the turn, decides whether a requested move is allowed, and tracks check, checkmate, and stalemate.
    GameController
    Connects the Swing window to the game (the Controller in Model-View-Controller).
    GameListener
    Receives notifications when a Game changes (Observer pattern).
    GameSettings
    The choices made in the new-game dialog: player names, and whether one side is played by the computer (and how well).
    GameStatus
    The state of a game from the point of view of the player whose turn it is.
    GameView
    What the GameController needs from the window.
    InputParser
    Converts raw text typed by the user into a Command.
    King
    A king: moves exactly one square in any direction, or castles.
    Knight
    A knight: moves in an "L" (two squares on one axis, one on the other) and may jump over any intervening pieces.
    LogConfig
    Sets up java.util.logging for the application.
    LogConfig.LineFormatter
    Formats each record on one line: 2026-11-24 17:55:01 INFO [Game] message.
    MinimaxStrategy
    A computer opponent that looks a fixed number of moves ahead using minimax search with alpha-beta pruning.
    Move
    A requested move: a source square, a destination square, and (for a pawn reaching the last rank) the piece type to promote to.
    MoveProblem
    The result of a piece's own movement check, returned by Piece.checkMove(chess.model.Position, chess.model.Board).
    MoveResult
    The outcome of an attempted move, returned by Game.tryMove(Position, Position).
    MoveStrategy
    A way of choosing a move for the computer opponent (Strategy pattern).
    MoveType
    What kind of move a Move turns out to be on a particular board.
    MoveValidator
    Decides whether a move is legal and, if not, explains why.
    NewGameDialog
    The "New Game" dialog: game mode, player names, and computer options.
    Pawn
    A pawn: moves forward one square into an empty square, or two squares from its starting rank if both squares are empty, and captures one square diagonally forward.
    Piece
    Abstract base class for all six chess piece types.
    PieceColor
    The two sides in a chess game.
    PieceFactory
    Creates pieces from a PieceType (Factory pattern).
    PieceGlyphs
    Maps pieces to Unicode chess symbols, so the GUI needs no image files.
    PieceType
    The six kinds of chess piece, with the data that does not depend on color.
    Player
    One of the two people playing the game.
    Position
    An immutable square on the 8 x 8 board.
    PromotionDialog
    Asks which piece a pawn reaching the last rank should become.
    Queen
    A queen: combines rook and bishop movement.
    RandomStrategy
    The easiest opponent: plays a uniformly random legal move.
    Rook
    A rook: moves any number of squares along a rank or file.
